title: Me llamo Ana
blurbEn: Your first text. Meet Ana, learn to say who you are and where you live, and see how Spanish gives every noun a gender.
body:
Hola. Me llamo Ana y soy de España. Vivo en Madrid.

Madrid es una ciudad grande. Mi casa es pequeña, pero es bonita.

Tengo un gato. Se llama Michi. Es un gato negro y muy simpático.

¿Y tú? ¿Cómo te llamas? ¿De dónde eres?
translationEn:
Hello. My name is Ana and I am from Spain. I live in Madrid.

Madrid is a big city. My house is small, but it is pretty.

I have a cat. His name is Michi. He is a black cat and very friendly.

And you? What is your name? Where are you from?

me.note: Reflexive pronoun. Spanish says 'I call myself Ana' rather than 'my name is Ana'.

una.note: Feminine form, because 'ciudad' is a feminine noun.

un.note: Masculine form, because 'gato' is a masculine noun.

pequeña.note: Ends in -a to agree with the feminine noun 'casa'.

phrases.note: Literally 'I call myself'. This is the standard way to introduce yourself.
Use 'ser' + 'de' to say where you are from.
Same pattern as 'me llamo', but about someone else.
